descriptionAdvanced.en: The Corocoro Mine is a storied and significant copper mining operation located in the arid highlands of the Pacajes Province, southwest of La Paz. It is historically famous for producing 'native copper' of exceptional purity, which was prized by both pre-Columbian cultures and colonial explorers. In the modern era, the mine has been revitalized through a partnership between the state mining company COMIBOL and international investors, utilizing advanced hydrometallurgical technology to produce high-grade copper cathodes. The city of Corocoro itself is a stark mining town that reflects a century of industrial effort and political struggle. Despite its remote and harsh Altiplano environment at nearly 4,000 meters, Corocoro remains the essential heart of Bolivia's copper industry and a key player in the nation's mineral diversification strategy.

en: Corocoro was once one of the most important copper-producing districts in the world during the early 20th century.
The mine's copper deposits are part of a unique geological formation typical of the central Altiplano.
The facility includes a modern 'electrowinning' plant for the processing of ore.
Historically, the town was a major station on the railway line between La Paz and Arica, Chile.
